localChanges: chore: update core-turn-based-game, core-game, core-save-game, core-spaceship, civ1-spaceship and civ1-player, and add civ1-game-end

log: Each ending is a named rule that calls core-turn-based-game's endGame: conquest once one civilization is left, the date at 2100 − 20 × level, the first spaceship to land, and the human defeated. The leader is warned once, 20 years before the end. game:over is emitted with the result, and a game nobody is playing carries on with its score final. lib/scoring has the end year, the conquest bonus, the rating and the famous leaders, from v474.05 (civ-clone/web-renderer#176, #177).

Review follow-ups: v474.05's turn is 0 at 4000 BC where ours is 1, so the bonus used to come out 2 points low. The README says that an ending part-way through a turn lets the others finish it, that the human destroyed waits for good, and what counts as someone playing.

As in v474.05, a computer player is defeated once it has no cities, and the human once they have no cities and no Settlers, which resolves the "total annihilation" TODOs. The defeat rules take the unit and client registries (civ-clone/web-renderer#176).

Review follow-up: losing a unit, a player with no cities is defeated only once it has no Settlers either. A computer player was defeated with the first unit it lost before founding its first city, which with conquest (civ-clone/web-renderer#176) could end a two-player game on turn 2. Losing its last city still defeats a computer player, as in v474.05.
chore: CI as the other engine repos run it, prettier --check, and drop the stale yarn lock file

Ships are checked once every player has moved, in player order, so the first player's ship wins a tie, and they always land. Capturing a city with a Palace loses its former owner's ship (back to Earth if it had launched, cancelled if not), as does the civilization being destroyed. player:spaceship:lost now says whether the ship had launched (civ-clone/web-renderer#177).
The Apollo Program now gives every civilization a ship, each on its own layout. It gave one only to the players still to move that turn, all sharing a single layout.

Review follow-ups: the arrival End rule is High priority, so a ship landing in the final year isn't beaten by the date ending whatever order the plugins load in. The Apollo Program test names its PlayerRegistry as one.
Rules/City/build.ts imports core-registry, core-science and core-wonder, and Rules/City/spend.ts base-city-yield-gold; only the yarn lock file's hoisting had found them (civ-clone/web-renderer#66).
From core-turn-based-game: how the game ended, once it has, so a game that carries on knows its score is final (civ-clone/web-renderer#176).
gameResult is runtime state (one GameResult). A file written before this has no gameResult membership and loads as a game still being played (civ-clone/web-renderer#176).
test: an ending with no winner round-trips
chore: CI as the other engine repos run it, prettier --check, and drop the stale lock file

check() no longer rolls the chance of success, which is left for a ruleset to score a landed ship by, so it draws no random number. lose() cancels a ship being built or one in flight, processing Lost. A lost ship being built is no longer the player's active one (civ-clone/web-renderer#177).
chore: CI as the other engine repos run it, prettier --check, and drop the unused core-yield and stale lock file

endGame records a GameResult (reason, winner, turn) once and processes the new GameOver rules with it. The turn loop now runs the End rules before the next turn starts, and waits there while a result's scoring isn't complete; game:continue resumes it, and turn:wait puts a loaded game back to waiting (civ-clone/web-renderer#176).
chore: the declarations as CI's TypeScript emits them
Review follow-ups: game:start resets the turn loop's waiting, GameResultRegistry takes the result it already holds without throwing, and the README names endGame's arguments as the code does.
